subject: Commercial structure for GenAssist per-token ladder and true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@genassist.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: GenAssist Procurement <procurement@genassist.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Hey Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the forecast through our internal model (attached) and wanted to align on two things before we get legal engaged:

1) Ladder shape: GenAssist prefers a marginal breakpoint ladder (i.e., each tranche priced at marginal rates) rather than a blended effective rate across all tokens. Our finance team argues marginal gives clearer signal on incremental cost.
2) True-up cadence & carry: we bill monthly but want clarity on how unused committed tokens are handled (carry-forward, credits, or forfeiture) and any quarterly true-up mechanics.

Can you sketch out a couple of clean options (marginal ladder with month-to-month true-up vs blended effective-rate with quarterly true-up) and note what Redwood recommends for a production API workload (latency-sensitive inference, bursty traffic)?

Attaching our volume profile.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Partnerships
GenAssist
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@genassist.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Liam —

Appreciate the model and the clarity. Quick summary from our side and two proposed structures attached:

Option A — Marginal ladder (recommended for high-variance growth):
- Breakpoints at 0-50M / 50-200M / 200M+ tokens per month
- Price applied to tokens in each tranche (marginal)
- Monthly true-up with quarter-end settlement; unused committed tokens carry forward for one quarter only
- Rationale: preserves predictability for both sides and keeps marginal economics aligned with actual usage spikes

Option B — Blended effective rate (recommended for predictable steady-state customers):
- Customer pays an effective blended $/k token based on expected monthly volume band
- Quarterly true-up and annual true-up adjustments; unused commit converted to credit on next invoice
- Rationale: simpler invoicing, but can obscure incremental cost signals during growth phases

Key caveats:
- We can support either but prefer marginal for bursty inference because it avoids surprise step-changes when you cross a breakpoint mid-month.
- We typically recommend a short carry-forward window (1 quarter) rather than indefinite credits to avoid exposure on our capacity planning.

I copied Marissa (commercial ops) and Karthik (billing/product) to help add any constraints from accounting and product. Attached a first-pass term sheet and a sample SLA PDF.

Next step: which option would GenAssist like to prototype in a POC billing run?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_SLA.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@genassist.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Quick operational notes from finance/ops:

- Invoicing cadence: Redwood invoices monthly on actual usage; committed discounts are applied as credits on the monthly invoice.
- True-up options we can offer in SOW: monthly true-up with quarterly settlement window OR quarterly only (no monthly true-up) — monthly true-up is operationally heavier but gives you faster alignment.
- Carry-forward mechanics we suggest: credits valid for two invoices (i.e., up to two months) or up to the following quarter for larger enterprise commits; this is negotiable by cohort.

Couple of asks for GenAssist to help us size the commit:
1) Can you share expected 3-, 6-, 12-month uplift scenarios (we saw the attached but a conservative and aggressive case would help)
2) Any regulatory constraints for audit/retention that would affect billing or data segregation?

I included a short pricing appendix in the attached redline of the term sheet.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: GenAssist_VOL_Model.xlsx (reference in email)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@genassist.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: GenAssist Procurement <procurement@genassist.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Thanks Marissa —

We can do conservative / base / upside scenarios and will post the spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow. A couple of clarifying points for Redwood:

- Procurement prefers a blended effective rate for contracting simplicity; platform team prefers marginal for signal. Could we do a hybrid: a marginal ladder with an option to surface an ``effective guaranteed rate`` for invoicing (i.e., Redwood calculates the blended $/k so our CFO sees a single line item) while preserving marginal calculation in the background for true-up and capacity?
- For carry-forward, GenAssist would advocate for carry through the quarter in case of seasonality between months.

Also, legal wants to understand penalty/credits if monthly usage wildly exceeds committed peak — e.g., is there a hard cap or automatic spike pricing?

—Liam
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@genassist.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Liam —

Hybrid approach is feasible. Implementation notes:

- Billing system will compute marginal pricing for each tranche to drive internal revenue recognition and capacity signals.
- We can expose an "effective guaranteed rate" on the invoice as a single-line summary (computed as blended $/k based on committed band). That invoice line will be informational but discounts/credits will be tied to the marginal computation behind the scenes.
- For overage: default is automatic spike billing at a pre-agreed overage rate (1.5x the marginal price of top tranche) unless you want an explicit hard cap with prior approval, in which case we can gate capacity but require a break-glass workflow.
- Carry-forward: default = carry through quarter-end (aligned with your ask). Credits beyond the quarter expire. For large multi-quarter commits we can extend carry term.

I'll draft the exact invoice example and a sample monthly true-up table and drop in the shared Drive by EOD.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Billing & Observability
Redwood Inference
From: GenAssist Procurement <procurement@genassist.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 17:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial ask: per-token ladder and true-up approach

Team —

Procurement is ok to proceed on a hybrid commercial structure as described, provided we get:

- A clean invoice example showing the single-line effective rate and the marginal breakdown in an appendix
- A cap/overage option and the language for break-glass escalation
- Confirmation that credits expire at quarter end unless otherwise agreed

Please send the sample invoice + term redline and we will route to legal for a quick review.

Thanks —
Elena Martínez
Senior Procurement Manager
GenAssist
